evidence.baseline: A cathedral is among the truest things human hands make and a cathedral is raised for what happens inside it. ... Everything built across these four volumes was, in the end, a structure shaped to hold a living presence it could not itself supply.
evidence.shipped: Those volumes described a cathedral of systems. This one asks what the cathedral is for.

The shipped pair states the topic of the image and deletes the image, which is 4.18's defect limb applied where its retention limb holds: the metaphor is carrying the argument, not decorating it.

findings.summary: The volume's own account of why it descends was replaced with a summary of the descent.

evidence.baseline: This is not the gentle volume. It is the load-bearing one. ... The future will not be built by institutions. It will be built by people who discover where they belong.
evidence.shipped: Institutions matter, but people build and inhabit them.

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.3, applied to the not X but Y construction.
findings.diagnosis: 4.3's retention limb applies. The rejected alternative, that institutions build the future, is the position most readers arrive holding, and the volume spends twenty chapters on the consequence of preferring it. Softening it to a concession removes the pressure the preface exists to create.

findings.summary: Two sentences of address to the reader were removed, and with them the volume's invitation to feel the argument before being told it.

evidence.baseline: Perhaps, somewhere near the end of the fourth volume, you felt it too ... If you did, stay with that feeling, because it is telling you something true.

findings.diagnosis: 4.16 forbids telling a reader what they already feel. The baseline hedges with perhaps and then makes the whole move conditional on if you did, which is the invitation the corpus card licenses rather than the conscription it forbids. The retention limb applies and the pass applied the defect limb.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.

The instructive case is the collision between R-LEDGER-WINS and a protected structural device: the pass paid down a status item by naming Purposeful and Providence in the preface, which the baseline withholds on purpose. audits.attributionInventory: Checked against the restored Volumes I through IV on 2026-07-31, inventoried only, nothing reconciled. HOLDS: the Volume IV description, translated that proposal into designs that can be examined and tested, matches Volume IV's own tested-in-thought and examined-under-pressure framing and respects CTD-0030 and CTD-0034; the Volume III description, a civilization grown this intricate requires a new architecture of coordination, is a fair paraphrase of Volume III's coordination-infrastructure and falling-coordination-capacity argument; ICONS, Individual Communities Observing Natural Sovereignty, and the Currency of Presence both stand verbatim in Volume I. PHANTOM OR OVERSTATED: the Volume I description, the first argued that coherence is the most viable substrate for a post-extractive civilization complex enough to survive itself, overstates Volume I, which at its line 43 assigns establishing whether coherence can function as a viable substrate to the academic documents and takes for itself the felt-and-recognized question; the Volume II description, intelligence is not a possession but a relationship, something that lives between minds rather than inside them, has no ancestor in the restored Volume II, Wielding Intelligence, whose nearest claim is the tendency statement that intelligence is increasingly collaborative, emergent, and distributed, so Volume V hardens a tendency into an ontology and attributes the result; the same family recurs at chapter three, the earlier volumes argued that intelligence itself is relational, at chapter seven, as the previous volumes argued with the ingredients-are-not-the-dish image no earlier volume uses, and at chapter ten, where the earlier work argued that coherence is the only durable substrate strengthens most viable to only durable, a claim Volume I nowhere makes. All flagged for the author; per CTD-0005 floor doctrine these are inconsistencies to call out, never reconcile, never encode.
audits.checked: R-LEDGER-WINS re-run: CTD-0034 remains open and the current fourth-volume sentence is the bounded form; restoring the baseline's can actually be built would reopen CTD-0030's C4, so it stays. R-PAIRED-DELETION: cathedral, arches, breath, substrate, and Donna swept two-ended; the arches protected line stands verbatim here and the cathedral returns in chapter sixteen. R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires. Title matter: the baseline's half-title line PURPOSEFUL, dropped by the pass, was restored above this section on 2026-07-31; the contents entries for chapters one and thirteen follow the settled heading renames and the part labels follow the census colon form, all verified against the structural census.
audits.prose: Glyphs normalized to the corpus straight convention per the volume anchor entry in v05-the-collaboration-problem; wording unchanged; the half-title restoration sits above this section's heading.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the twenty rules. Ten of thirty-eight baseline sentences do not survive and every one is attributed to a recorded decision or a glyph repair. The attribution inventory finds two phantom-strength descriptions, Volumes I and II, and flags them without reconciling.
